findings.description: Login-cache invalidation on update is skipped when the org-aware wrapped `original` reports isEnabled()=false (e.g. organization disabled), leaving stale IDPs in the getForLogin cache after updates that should remove them. — WHAT: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate tests getLoginPredicate() against `original`, which update() obtains from getById() — a method that always returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...), i.e. an org-aware wrapped model whose isEnabled() can be false even when the stored IDP is enabled (this PR's own bean change, 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped', proves wrapping alters isEnabled). The cached login sets are built from idpDelegate.getForLogin (raw DB state), so membership is based on the stored flags, not the wrapped ones. WHY: when the IDP's organization is disabled, predicate(original) is false although the IDP IS in the cached login set; if an admin update during that window makes the raw updated model also fail the predicate (hide_on_login=true, broker_public=false, link_only=true), line 405 skips invalidation, the stale id stays in the login cache, and because the login-page bean only re-checks isEnabled (not hideOnLogin/BROKER_PUBLIC), the IDP wrongly reappears on the login page once the organization is re-enabled — the admin's change silently never takes effect for the cached login views. HOW: compute the predicate for `original` from the unwrapped stored model (e.g. use idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId()) for the comparison, or add a variant of createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel that exposes the raw model) so the before/after comparison uses the same unwrapped state that determines cache membership.

The login cache accumulates one id set per distinct organizationId inside a single cluster-replicated cache entry with no eviction, causing unbounded growth and O(N) copy on every new organization's first login. — WHAT: getForLogin caches all results under a single revisioned entry per (realm, FetchMode), keyed internally by searchKey = organizationId (or ""), and every distinct organization that renders a login page permanently appends a new Set<String> of internal IDP ids to that one cache value via the merging IdentityProviderListQuery constructor (putAll(previous.searchKeys)); entries are never individually evicted. WHY: in realms with many organizations the entry grows unboundedly (N orgs × the full realm-level login IDP id set duplicated into each org's set), is replicated across the Infinispan cluster on every change, and each first-time login for a new organization performs an O(accumulated-size) map copy plus invalidateObject on the login hot path — total copy work grows quadratically with organization count. HOW: cap the number of cached searchKeys (e.g. only cache the null/"" organization result and serve per-organization ALL queries from the delegate, or bound the map with an LRU-style eviction by re-creating the query without the oldest key), or key the cache by (realm, mode, organizationId) so entries stay small and independently evictable.

Invalidation predicate excludes org-linked non-public brokers even though getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId) returns them, leaving the new login caches stale when such brokers are created, removed, enabled, or hidden. — WHAT: the new getLoginPredicate() clause `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` makes the Infinispan invalidation helpers (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) treat organization-linked non-public brokers as non-login IDPs, but getForLogin(ALL, orgId) and getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, orgId) (default method, lines 176-178) return exactly those brokers for members of that organization. WHY: creating, deleting, enabling/disabling, or toggling hideOnLogin/linkOnly on an org-private broker no longer invalidates the `.idp.login.ALL` / `.idp.login.ORG_ONLY` cache entries introduced by this PR, so organization members see a stale broker list on the login page (a newly enabled or newly linked private broker never appears; a broker switched to hideOnLogin stays visible because the bean only re-filters isEnabled) — behavior that was always fresh before this caching layer existed. HOW: drop the org-visibility clause from the predicate used for invalidation (keep only Objects::nonNull plus the LoginFilter reduce), so any login-eligible IDP change invalidates the per-FetchMode login caches; over-invalidation is safe here, under-invalidation is not.

Client deletion crashes with UnsupportedOperationException when FGAC v2 is enabled because the removal listener now routes into the throwing ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled stub — WHAT: The new clients() override makes the AdminPermissions.registerListener ClientRemovedEvent handler call ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and the listener (guarded by the V1 feature, which V2 implies) fires synchronously during client deletion, so deleting any client — and realm deletion, which removes clients — fails with a 500 and the transaction rolls back; before this PR the listener used V1 ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled, which performs the cleanup. HOW: Make ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled tolerate the disable path invoked by system listeners (e.g., no-op or delete the client's authorization resources/policies when enable=false) instead of throwing unconditionally.

getClientsWithPermission relies on findByType("Clients") but V2 per-client resources are created without a type, so per-client permissions are never listed — WHAT: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...), but the V2 per-client resource creation path (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) creates resources via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) without ever calling setType, unlike V1 ClientPermissions.initialize which explicitly sets resource.setType("Client"). WHY: If per-client resources carry no type, findByType matches nothing and the method always returns an empty set, so its caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229 silently filters out all clients for fine-grained admins; additionally the all-clients type resource (named "Clients") is not excluded from the iteration and can leak into the returned ID set. HOW: Set the type on per-client resources at creation (resource.setType(resourceType) in getOrCreateResource) and skip the type resource (resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) inside the findByType consumer.

hasPermission passes a possibly-null all-clients type resource to findByResource on realms lacking the new Clients type resource — WHAT: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), when the per-client resource is absent, the fallback AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) can return null (the "Clients" type resource does not exist for realms that enabled admin permissions before this PR introduced the type), and the result is passed straight into authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. WHY: If findByResource dereferences the resource (e.g., resource.getId() in the JPA store), every canManage/canView/canConfigure(client) evaluation for an admin without the manage-clents realm role throws a NullPointerException on such realms. HOW: Return false when the fallback type resource is null before calling findByResource.

MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override exposes throwing ClientPermissionsV2 stubs (UnsupportedOperationException) to pre-existing callers such as ClientResource.getManagementPermissions (lines 705-720). — Recorded finding #1: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override exposes the new ClientPermissionsV2 stubs to pre-existing callers. Verified via grep that ClientResource.getManagementPermissions (management/permissions endpoint, lines 705-720) calls isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions, which throw UnsupportedOperationException in the new ClientPermissionsV2, so this pre-existing endpoint now fails at runtime through the same changed line.

V1 stores per-client resources with type "Client" but V2 getClientsWithPermission queries findByType("Clients"), so the V2 query misses the V1-created resources. — Recorded finding #2: Resource type mismatch — V1 creates per-client resources with setType("Client") while V2 getClientsWithPermission queries findByType("Clients"), so the V2 query will not match the resources created under V1. The per-resource evaluatePermission loop noted in the performance review sits on these same lines and is not a distinct issue.

The getResourceTypeResource fallback in hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) can be null, creating a null-dereference risk. — Recorded finding #3: Null-risk fallback — hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) falls back to getResourceTypeResource, which may return null, creating a null-dereference risk in that path.

Team admins/owners are always denied because the admin and owner checks are ANDed instead of ORed. — WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin() and isTeamOwner() with && instead of ||. WHY: a team membership has exactly one role, so no user can be both ADMIN and OWNER at once — the expression is always false, and team admins/owners (who are neither the organizer nor an attendee) always get FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to team event bookings. HOW: replace && with ||.

Calendar attendee update uses the requester's credentials rather than the organizer's, so it targets the wrong user's calendars for non-organizer callers. — WHAT: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and {...user}) instead of the booking organizer's. WHY: the calendar event being updated lives on the organizer's calendar, so when an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) adds guests, the attendee/credential lookup runs against the wrong user's connected calendars and the organizer's calendar event is not updated — the handler even includes booking.user.credentials at line 38 but never uses them. HOW: build the EventManager from booking.user and its credentials instead of ctx.user.

Call to EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees has no discoverable definition in the repo, risking a TypeError after the attendee rows are already committed. — WHAT: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) is called, but a repo-wide search finds no definition of updateCalendarAttendees (or of the EventManager class) anywhere — the only match is this call site. WHY: if the method does not exist on EventManager, every addGuests call throws a TypeError after prisma.booking.update has already persisted the new attendees, returning a 500 while leaving guests added and no calendar/email side effects. HOW: verify the method exists on @calcom/core/EventManager (or add it / call the correct existing method) and handle its failure before or transactionally with the attendee insert.

Guest blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing trivial bypass and duplicate attendees. — WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is never lowercased before the includes() check. WHY: a blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g., Banned@x.com vs banned@x.com) bypasses the blacklist and is added as an attendee; the adjacent duplicate check (guest === attendee.email) is likewise case-sensitive and can create duplicate attendee rows for the same mailbox. HOW: normalize with guest.toLowerCase() in both the blacklist comparison and the existing-attendee comparison.

Raw input guest list is sent to the email routine instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, re-emailing existing attendees. — WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input guests array instead of uniqueGuests. WHY: the callee (packages/emails/email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails) emails every booking attendee whose email appears in that list, so any pre-existing attendee emails included in the request receive a 'new guests added' notification even though they were not added by this call. HOW: pass uniqueGuests instead of guests.

Guests can be added to cancelled bookings because the booking fetch ignores status. — WHAT: the booking lookup does not filter on booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled (or otherwise non-active) bookings. WHY: attendees are persisted and 'guests added' calendar-invite emails are sent for an event that no longer exists, misleading the new guests and mutating a cancelled record. HOW: add a status check (e.g., reject when booking.status === BookingStatus.CANCELLED/REJECTED) before updating.

Null booking.userId falls back to id 0 in findFirstOrThrow, causing an unhandled 500 for team bookings without an assigned user. — WHAT: the organizer is loaded with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }), which throws when booking.userId is null. WHY: bookings without an assigned user (e.g., collective team bookings where userId is null) hit the id: 0 fallback, findFirstOrThrow throws, and the mutation fails with a 500 instead of a controlled error — even for callers who passed the permission check. HOW: handle the null userId case explicitly (resolve the team host or throw a typed TRPCError).

Adding guests bypasses the seatsPerTimeSlot capacity limit for seated event types. — WHAT: new attendees are created via createMany without any check against eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot. WHY: for events with seats enabled, seatsPerTimeSlot is a hard capacity invariant — this endpoint lets any existing attendee add unlimited guests and overbook the slot beyond its seat limit, which the normal booking flow enforces. HOW: when seatsPerTimeSlot is set, reject if existing attendee count + uniqueGuests.length would exceed it.

Duplicate emails within the guests array are not deduplicated, so createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows for the same booking and the guest is emailed multiple times. — WHAT: uniqueGuests is not deduplicated within the input array itself — the filter only excludes emails already on the booking or blacklisted, so duplicate emails inside the same guests payload all pass through to createMany. WHY: submitting guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] creates two Attendee rows with the same email on the same booking (verified: the Attendee model in packages/prisma/schema.prisma has no @@unique([bookingId, email]) constraint, so nothing at the DB layer prevents it), and sendAddGuestsEmails then emails that guest twice — the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' invariant the handler claims to enforce is not actually upheld. HOW: dedupe the input before filtering, e.g. wrap guests in a Set first.

Prefix/suffix trimming in the new diff-reporting code can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the build instead of reporting illegal HTML. — WHAT: the prefix/suffix trimming loops that build the 'Illegal HTML' diagnostic are only bounded individually, so start + end can overlap and substring() is invoked with begin > end. WHY: when the sanitizer strips a trailing fragment whose tail coincidentally matches the kept content (e.g. value 'x' sanitizes to 'x', producing start=8 and end=4 so sanitized.substring(8, 4) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException), the Maven build crashes with an obscure stack trace instead of reporting the illegal HTML, and no further keys or files are validated. HOW: clamp the end loop so the trimmed regions cannot overlap, e.g. while (end < sanitized.length() - start && end < value.length() - start && ...).

Locale-suffix regex has an accidental Z–_ range and excludes digits/hyphens, so such locale files would not resolve to the English bundle and would crash the build. — WHAT: the locale-stripping regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' uses a character class that is accidentally the range Z–_ (matching [, \, ], ^, _) and excludes digits and hyphens. WHY: a locale file whose suffix contains digits or hyphens (e.g. messages_es_419.properties) would not match, so englishFile keeps the same locale filename under resources/ instead of _en.properties, producing a FileNotFoundException wrapped in RuntimeException that crashes the build; the unintended range characters are also matched. HOW: use an explicit class such as '_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\.properties' (or '_[^_]*\.properties') to cover all locale suffixes.

The prefix and suffix trimming loops at lines 103-111 overlap, causing the shared region to be processed by both loops. — The prefix and suffix trimming loops at lines 103-111 overlap: the two loops' ranges share a common region, so trimming is applied to the same characters by both loops. Adjust the loop bounds so the prefix-trimming and suffix-trimming regions are disjoint.

The locale-stripping regex at line 75 accidentally forms a Z-_ character-class range that matches unintended characters. — The locale-stripping regex at line 75 contains an accidental Z-_ range in its character class: the hyphen is interpreted as a range operator between 'Z' and '_', so the class also matches unintended characters ('[', '\\', ']', '^'). Escape the hyphen or move it to the start/end of the character class so only the intended characters are matched.

Non-atomic count-then-insert lets concurrent anonymous requests exceed the configured device limit. — WHAT: the device-limit enforcement in CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a non-atomic check-then-act: CountDevices (SELECT COUNT(*)) followed by a conditional INSERT outside any transaction or lock. WHY: concurrent anonymous auth requests (TagDevice now runs synchronously in every request, see client.go:44) can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, so the configured device limit is silently exceeded — undermining the limit this PR adds. HOW: enforce the limit atomically, e.g. run the count check and the insert inside a single transaction with appropriate isolation (or use a single conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit statement).

Failing anonymous auth on device-limit errors lets unauthenticated clients exhaust client-controlled device slots and deny service to legitimate anonymous users for 30+ days. — WHAT: anonymous authentication now hard-fails when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, while the device IDs that consume limit slots come from the unauthenticated, client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header (impl.go:119) and occupied slots count against the limit for 30 days (anonymousDeviceExpiration window used by CountDevices in database.go:110). WHY: an unauthenticated attacker can send requests with random device IDs to exhaust all device_limit slots; every legitimate new anonymous user then gets an authentication error (HTTP 401) instead of access, for up to 30+ days — before this PR tagging was fire-and-forget and could never block authentication. HOW: distinguish 'new device rejected by limit' from auth failure (log and continue authenticating, as done for other tagging errors), or validate/rate-limit device-ID claims before persisting them so unauthenticated clients cannot burn the licensed capacity.

Rejected over-limit devices are only rejected once: the failed tag attempt leaves a 29-minute local-cache entry, so a simple retry authenticates and bypasses the configured device limit. — WHAT: failing anonymous auth on ErrDeviceLimitReached (new in this PR) is bypassed on retry because tagDeviceUI in impl.go sets the local cache key (a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) at impl.go:146, 29-minute TTL) BEFORE calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it when CreateOrUpdateDevice fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached. WHY: a new device over the limit is rejected only on its first request; any retry within 29 minutes hits the cache at impl.go:142-144, tagDeviceUI returns nil without touching the DB, and Authenticate succeeds — so the configurable device limit this PR adds is effectively unenforced against every client that retries (enforcement degenerates to failing one request per device ID per 29-minute window). HOW: on error from CreateOrUpdateDevice in tagDeviceUI (impl.go:152-154), delete the cache key before returning the error (e.g. a.localCache.Delete(key)), so failed tags are retried against the store and ErrDeviceLimitReached is enforced on every request.

Async legacy writes inherit the request context, so they are canceled as soon as the HTTP handler returns and the legacy mirror write is silently dropped. — WHAT: the fire-and-forget goroutine derives its context from the incoming request ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). WHY: DualWriter is a rest.Storage invoked synchronously from apiserver REST handlers (dualwriter.go:127-178), so ctx is the HTTP request context, which net/http cancels the moment the handler returns — the async legacy Create returns immediately with context.Canceled and the legacy mirror write is silently lost, defeating mode 3's 'safe measure' purpose; the same pattern exists in Delete (lines 108-114), Update (lines 134-141) and DeleteCollection (lines 161-167). HOW: detach from request cancellation before applying the timeout, e.g. ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, errors.New("legacy create timeout")) (keeps klog values set by klog.NewContext while dropping cancellation).

Storage Create/Update failures are recorded against the legacy metrics histogram instead of the storage one. — WHAT: on failure of d.Storage.Create, the error path calls d.recordLegacyDuration(...) instead of d.recordStorageDuration(...). WHY: metrics.go:54-62 shows legacy and storage are separate HistogramVecs, so a storage failure is recorded as a legacy error (with storage timing) and the storage error metric is never observed — dashboards/alerts for mode 3 attribute failures to the wrong backend; the identical mistake exists in Update's error path at lines 127-130 (d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) after d.Storage.Update fails). HOW: replace with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) in both error paths.

Delete records the per-object name into the Prometheus `kind` label, creating unbounded time-series cardinality. — WHAT: the success path of Delete passes the object `name` as the third argument to recordStorageDuration, which metrics.go:59-62 maps into the `kind` label of the dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds histogram (label set defined as {"is_error","mode","kind","method"} at metrics.go:23). WHY: every distinct object name creates a new Prometheus time series — unbounded label cardinality that grows with the number of deleted objects and can blow up the metrics store, and every other method passes options.Kind so the label is also semantically wrong. HOW: use d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

DeleteCollection records the legacy store's duration/errors into the storage metrics histogram. — WHAT: inside DeleteCollection's async goroutine, the result of d.Legacy.DeleteCollection is recorded with d.recordStorageDuration instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. WHY: legacy delete-collection latency and errors are attributed to the storage histogram while the legacy histogram never observes them, corrupting the per-backend duration/error metrics that the dual-writer rollout relies on (verified the two recorders write to separate HistogramVecs in metrics.go:54-62). HOW: change to d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

Legacy Update recomputes UpdatedObject from its own old object instead of reusing the storage-updated object, so legacy and unified storage can silently diverge. — WHAT: Update now passes the raw objInfo to d.Legacy.Update; the removed code pre-resolved the object (Storage.Get + objInfo.UpdatedObject) and wrapped it in updateWrapper (dualwriter.go:222-238, whose UpdatedObject returns the fixed pre-computed object) so legacy persisted the exact object storage wrote. WHY: rest.UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is now executed a second time, inside the legacy store, against legacy's own old object — if legacy's copy is stale (the common case during migration) or the objInfo applies mutations, legacy writes different content than unified storage, so the two backends this mode is meant to keep in sync diverge silently; objInfo implementations are also not guaranteed to be safe/idempotent across two UpdatedObject invocations. HOW: resolve the updated object once (as the old code did, e.g. via d.Storage.Get + objInfo.UpdatedObject before calling Storage.Update) and pass &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj} to d.Legacy.Update.

Update error path records the storage failure into the legacy metrics histogram instead of the storage one. — WHAT: the error branch of Update records the failed d.Storage.Update duration via d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration. WHY: storage update failures are observed in the legacy duration histogram (wrong metric vector) and are never counted in the storage duration histogram, making storage-side update error rates invisible in monitoring. HOW: call d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) in this branch, matching the success path two lines below.

Mode3 tests never await or assert the async legacy write, so the legacy dual-write could be removed without failing any test. — WHAT: the mode3 tests register legacy mock expectations (setupLegacyFn) but never synchronize with or assert the fire-and-forget goroutine that performs the legacy write — dw.Create/dw.Update return before the goroutine runs and no AssertExpectations/WaitGroup/channel is used. WHY: the async legacy dual-write, the core safety behavior of mode 3, is effectively untested: removing every legacy `go func(){...}()` block from dualwriter_mode3.go would leave this entire suite green, so a regression that silently drops legacy writes cannot be caught. HOW: have the tests signal completion from the legacy mock (e.g., a channel closed inside a .Run callback) and wait on it, plus m.AssertExpectations(t), before asserting results.

raw_html cook_method serves unsanitized third-party feed HTML as cooked post content, enabling stored XSS from RSS imports. — WHAT: For posts with cook_method == raw_html, cook returns the raw column verbatim as the served HTML, bypassing PrettyText's whitelist sanitizer and the :after_post_cook plugin filter. WHY: Combined with PollFeed doing CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) (poll_feed.rb:35) and TopicEmbed.import passing no sanitization, third-party RSS feed entries become stored, unsanitized HTML on Discourse topic pages — a compromised or malicious feed on the embeddable host can inject <script> and steal sessions of Discourse readers, including staff. HOW: Sanitize imported content before storing (e.g. run contents through a whitelist sanitizer such as Sanitize/PrettyText in TopicEmbed.import), or have cook still sanitize raw_html instead of returning it raw.

embed.post is used unguarded; a destroyed post makes revise! raise NoMethodError and aborts the whole feed poll loop. — WHAT: When a TopicEmbed record exists, the code uses embed.post without a nil guard and passes it straight into PostRevisor.new / revise!. WHY: If the post was destroyed after the embed was created (no dependent-destroy wiring on TopicEmbed/Post for this association), embed.post is nil, revise! raises NoMethodError, and — because PollFeed#poll_feed loops over all feed items calling import — one stale embed record aborts the entire hourly feed poll (sidekiq retry is disabled). HOW: Skip or recreate when the post is missing.

content_sha1 is updated even when the revision fails, permanently suppressing future content updates for that embed. — WHAT: content_sha1 is persisted via embed.update_column regardless of whether revisor.revise! actually applied the new content. WHY: If the revision fails (revise! returns false instead of raising), the embed row now records the NEW sha while the post still has the OLD body — every subsequent poll computes the same new sha, sees content_sha1 == embed.content_sha1, and skips the update, so the post stays stale permanently. HOW: Only update the sha when the revision succeeds.

Feed items without a content element cause nil.scrub NoMethodError that aborts the entire hourly poll. — WHAT: i.content.scrub assumes every feed item has a content element; SimpleRSS returns nil for elements absent from an item (e.g. RSS 2.0 items that only carry description). WHY: nil.scrub raises NoMethodError, which propagates out of poll_feed and kills the entire hourly job mid-loop — with sidekiq_options retry: false the remaining items are never imported until the next run, which then dies on the same item again. HOW: Coerce to string or skip items without content.

Non-atomic setnx+expire can leave a permanent throttle key, blocking retrieval of that embed URL forever. — WHAT: The throttle key is written with setnx and then given a TTL in a separate expire call, which is not atomic. WHY: If the process crashes or is killed between the two calls, the key "retrieved:<url>" exists forever with no expiry, so that embed URL is permanently treated as retrieved_recently? and can never be fetched again. HOW: Set the value and TTL atomically.

open-uri calls in Sidekiq workers have no timeout, so an unresponsive feed/embed host can hang worker threads indefinitely. — WHAT: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) (and open(url) in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout inside Sidekiq job workers. WHY: An unresponsive or slow embeddable host blocks a worker thread indefinitely; with hourly polling plus per-URL retrieve jobs, a hanging host progressively exhausts the Sidekiq worker pool and stalls all other jobs. HOW: Fetch with explicit timeouts (e.g. Net::HTTP with open_timeout/read_timeout, or Timeout.timeout) and rescue network errors so one bad host cannot hang the queue.

Protocol-relative URLs (//host/path) in imported content are mangled into invalid same-host paths. — WHAT: absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.example.com/img.png') as path-relative because they satisfy start_with?('/'), rewriting them to 'http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png'. WHY: any feed or article using protocol-relative links/images (common in RSS content) gets broken links and broken images in the imported post. HOW: exclude '//'-prefixed values from the rewrite.

Port is wrongly omitted for non-default scheme/port combinations (http on 443, https on 80). — WHAT: The port-elision check drops the port whenever it equals 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, so 'https://host:80' or 'http://host:443' produce a prefix missing the non-default port. WHY: absolutize_urls then generates absolute links pointing at the wrong port, breaking links/images for embeddable hosts running on a non-default scheme/port combination. HOW: compare against the scheme's default port instead of hardcoding both values.

Each new embed URL synchronously re-downloads and re-imports the entire RSS feed inside a user-triggerable job. — WHAT: perform_retrieve executes the full Jobs::PollFeed synchronously for every cache-miss embed URL when feed polling is enabled. WHY: the retrieved_recently? throttle is keyed per embed_url, so N distinct article URLs each trigger a complete feed download plus a TopicEmbed.import scan of every feed item inside a job enqueued by the public EmbedController#best endpoint — O(N × feed size) network and import work driven by unauthenticated traffic to the embedded site. HOW: rely on the hourly scheduled PollFeed (remove the inline execute), or enqueue a single coalesced poll job instead of running it inline per request.

Check-then-create on embed_url without a unique constraint allows duplicate topics for the same embed URL under concurrent imports. — WHAT: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-create (where(embed_url: url).first followed by TopicEmbed.create! inside the transaction) with no uniqueness guarantee on embed_url. WHY: the hourly PollFeed has no throttle and can run concurrently with RetrieveTopic.fetch_http for the same new URL (RetrieveTopic even runs PollFeed itself), and staff bypass the redis throttle, so two concurrent imports can create duplicate topics and duplicate TopicEmbed rows for the same embed_url. HOW: add a unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and use find_or_create_by (or rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and reload).

onEnable() was removed from the success path and only fires via the Close button, so dismissing the backup-codes dialog any other way leaves parent state stale (2FA shown as disabled) and the modal unrestarted. — WHAT: After a successful 2FA enable (response.status === 200), onEnable() is no longer called here — it only fires from the Close button on the DisplayBackupCodes step. WHY: If the user dismisses the dialog via the X button, overlay click, or Escape (all routed through onOpenChange, line 166) instead of the Close button, the parent is never notified that 2FA was enabled, so the settings UI keeps showing 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled server-side; additionally resetState() is never called, so reopening the modal lands on the stale backup-codes step instead of ConfirmPassword. HOW: Fire onEnable() immediately upon the successful enable response (keep DisplayBackupCodes purely informational), or invoke onEnable() + resetState() from the dialog's onOpenChange handler whenever the current step is DisplayBackupCodes.

Non-atomic check-then-consume of backup codes allows two concurrent login requests to redeem the same one-time backup code. — WHAT: Backup-code redemption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the encrypted blob is decrypted, the code is located with indexOf, and only afterwards is the nulled-out array written back with prisma.user.update. WHY: Two concurrent authorize() calls presenting the same backup code both read the same ciphertext and both pass the indexOf check before either update commits, so a one-time backup code can be used twice; the per-email rate limiter throttles attempts but does not serialize concurrent in-flight requests. HOW: Make the claim atomic — e.g. run the check-and-consume inside a serializable transaction (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), or use updateMany({ where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, data: {...} }) and reject when count === 0 because a concurrent request already consumed the code.

New error codes ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode / MissingBackupCodes are referenced in four files but no definition was found — compile error if ErrorCode is an enum, undefined error values if it is an object. — WHAT: This PR references ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes and ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode (also in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:55,63 and the two modals), but ErrorCode.ts is not part of this diff and my repo-wide search for these identifiers found only the usages, never a definition. Org/team authorization SQL is returned with a top-level OR and no enclosing parentheses, so composing it with additional ANDed filters breaks precedence and widens the authorization condition. — WHAT: getBaseConditions (and getAuthorizationConditions) can return a raw SQL fragment containing a top-level OR — e.g. `("teamId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)` produced by the reducers at lines 171-174/204-207 and returned unwrapped at lines 74-77 when filterConditions is null. WHY: the previous WhereInput return type was structurally safe to compose, but a raw fragment with a top-level OR silently breaks precedence for any consumer that embeds it as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra filters>` — AND binds tighter than OR, turning `(authA) OR (authB) AND extra` into `authA OR (authB AND extra)`, which widens the authorization clause and returns bookings outside the intended filters. HOW: always wrap the composed result in parentheses, e.g. make the reducers return `Prisma.sql`(${joined})`` or have getBaseConditions/getAuthorizationConditions return `Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`` so the fragment is safe to embed.

The filter-only branch in getBaseConditions is dead code because authorization conditions are never null, masking the assumption that denial could be a falsy value. — WHAT: the `else if (filterConditions)` branch in getBaseConditions is unreachable — getAuthorizationConditions() is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and every code path (including deny and invalid-options paths) returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, so `authConditions` is always truthy. WHY: dead code indicates a logic mistake (the author appears to have assumed auth conditions could be null as in the old API where the array was filtered for null); behavior is currently correct only because denial is expressed as the truthy `1=0` fragment, and future refactors that return null for deny would silently drop the authorization constraint via this branch. HOW: remove the dead branch or restructure so the deny case is explicit, e.g. combine only non-null filter conditions with the always-present auth condition.

getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized top-level OR fragment, which will compose incorrectly (and break authorization scoping) if any caller appends an AND condition. — getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized top-level OR fragment (lines 118-119, produced by the reduces at 215-218 and 248-251). If any caller ever appends an AND condition to this fragment, operator precedence will break the intended authorization scoping, so the OR fragment should be wrapped in parentheses. The else-if/else null-handling branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions() never returns null. — The else-if/else branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable dead code because getAuthorizationConditions() never returns null, so the null-handling paths can never execute. Dataclass field `queued` uses import-time `timezone.now()` default instead of `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`, giving every instance a stale timestamp. — WHAT: the `queued` field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the dataclass is defined (at module import), not each time an AssignmentSource is created. WHY: every AssignmentSource produced by from_integration() silently carries the process-import timestamp instead of the time the assignment was actually queued, so any consumer of `queued` (logging, latency measurement, or future cycle-detection logic) reads a permanently stale value. MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class wired as MetricAlertFire's detector_handler, crashing any detector of that type at runtime. — WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so the class cannot be instantiated. WHY: StatefulDetectorHandler enforces these via abc.ABC, and MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler means Detector.detector_handler (which calls group_type.detector_handler(self)) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any detector of type metric_alert_fire processed by process_detectors — previously the handler was instantiable and evaluate() returned []. HOW: either implement the four abstract methods on MetricAlertDetectorHandler (even as stubs returning empty values, e.g. counter_names = [], get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values returning trivial values, build_occurrence_and_event_data raising NotImplementedError), or keep it subclassing DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation lands.

Duplicate downsize definition overrides the 4-positional-arg version, breaking Jobs::ResizeEmoji which still calls it with 5 arguments. — WHAT: The diff adds a second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` definition while leaving the original `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in place, so Ruby discards the 5-argument version. WHY: `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, which now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)` — every emoji resize job crashes. HOW: Delete the dead 4-arg downsize definition and update resize_emoji.rb to the new contract: `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "100x100", opts)`.

Animated-GIF detection keys off the tempfile path extension, which browser multipart tempfiles lack, so auto-downsized animated GIFs are silently flattened to a static first frame. — WHAT: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with `tempfile.path`, but the animated-GIF branch in `optimize` only triggers when the `from` path matches /\.GIF$/i — and for normal browser uploads `file.tempfile` is a Rack multipart tempfile with no file extension (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart123). WHY: animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb that are uploaded through the composer go through `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame — animation is silently destroyed even though the site has allow_animated_thumbnails enabled and the code explicitly passes allow_animation. Only API URL downloads work, because FileHelper.download appends the original extension to its tempfile. HOW: give the tempfile a path carrying the original extension before downsizing so the GIF detection in optimize can match.

Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit drops per-type site settings, breaking attachment validation and sites with image limits above 10MB. — WHAT: The client-side size check now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` for every upload, replacing the per-type `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup (and the 413 handler at line 246 hardcodes 10MB in the error message too). WHY: attachments are no longer validated against max_attachment_size_kb client-side — users can select oversized attachments that only fail after a full server round-trip — and sites configured with max_image_size_kb above 10MB now have legitimate image uploads blocked by the browser even though the server would accept them; the 413 message also reports a wrong limit whenever the configured limit differs from 10MB. HOW: keep the 10MB ceiling for images (matching the new server-side downsize budget) but retain the site setting for attachments.

update/destroy crash with NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 when the embeddable host id does not exist. — WHAT: update and destroy look up the host with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call host.destroy / save_host(host) without a nil check. WHY: for an unknown or stale id (double-delete, outdated admin list, direct API call) host is nil, so nil.destroy at line 16 and nil.host= inside save_host at line 23 raise NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: raise Discourse::NotFound when the record is missing before touching it.

before_validation crashes with NoMethodError on nil host instead of producing a validation error. — WHAT: the before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! twice without guarding against a nil host. WHY: when create/update is submitted without params[:embeddable_host][:host] (or any code saves an EmbeddableHost with host unset), nil.sub! raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of surfacing the format validation error. HOW: coerce/guard before normalizing, e.g. assign via self.host = host.to_s.sub(...).sub(...) so nil becomes an empty string that fails validation cleanly.

Hosts saved with a port pass validation but can never match in record_for_host because uri.host strips the port. — WHAT: the validation regex (line 2) explicitly allows a port (:[0-9]{1,5})? in the stored host, but record_for_host looks up records using only uri.host, which never includes the port. WHY: an admin can successfully save 'example.com:3000', yet EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? will never match referers from that origin, so embedding from any host on a non-default port is silently rejected and TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:36) never finds its category. HOW: include the port in the lookup key when present, e.g. build the candidate as uri.host plus ":#{uri.port}" for non-default ports and match either form, or strip the port at save time and reject storing one.

EmbeddingController#update silently ignores all input and changes nothing while returning success. — WHAT: the update action is identical to show — it renders the freshly built @embedding OpenStruct and never reads or persists any params. WHY: any client (admin UI or API consumer) that PUTs embedding changes receives a successful response while nothing is saved, a silent contract break for an endpoint named update. HOW: remove the update action until there is something to persist, or have it apply the submitted attributes before rendering.

Host validation regex rejects valid domains with TLDs longer than 5 chars or punycode double-hyphen labels — WHAT: the host validation regex restricts the TLD to 2-5 lowercase letters ([a-z]{2,5}) and permits only a single hyphen or dot between labels ([\-\.]{1}). WHY: valid hostnames with TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. example.technology, example.museum, example.international) and punycode/IDN labels containing double hyphens (e.g. xn--nxasmq6b.example) fail validation, so admins cannot register those sites as embeddable hosts and embedding is silently broken for them. HOW: relax the regex, e.g. widen the TLD group to [a-z]{2,} (or [a-z]{2,63}) and allow multiple hyphens per label, e.g. /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.][a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i.

New per-site fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale) is not part of the translate accelerator's process-global LRU cache key, so fallback translations leak across multisite sites with different default locales and go stale on locale changes. — WHAT: The new fallback chain makes I18n.t results depend on SiteSetting.default_locale (per-site in multisite), but lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 caches zero-arg translations in a process-global LRU keyed only by "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" — the fallback chain/site is not part of the key. WHY: In a multisite cluster where two sites have different default_locale, a key missing in the requested locale resolves through different fallback chains per site, but whichever result is cached first is served to the other site until the 300-entry LRU evicts it — users see text in the wrong fallback language, nondeterministically; the same stale cache serves the old fallback language after an admin changes default_locale at runtime. HOW: Include the fallback chain (or SiteSetting.default_locale) in the cache key in translate_accelerator.rb, e.g. k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{SiteSetting.default_locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", or bypass the cache for lookups that miss in the primary locale.

getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null on concurrent deletion, propagating a nullable result to GroupRepresentation and any unboxing caller without an audited contract. — WHAT: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the delegate lookup returns null (concurrent group deletion), changing the method's contract from non-null count to nullable without any audit of the callers. WHY: the only caller visible in this checkout (GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount) passes the value to representation.setSubGroupCount(...) so null propagates silently into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount and out through the admin REST API, and any other consumer of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() that unboxes the Long (assignment to long, comparison such as count > 0, arithmetic) will throw the very NPE this PR is meant to eliminate; note that every other 'group not found' path in this same class (getDelegateForUpdate, isUpdated) throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") rather than returning null, so this is also an inconsistent failure mode. HOW: either mark GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() as nullable in the interface and verify every caller tolerates null (no unboxing), or throw the same IllegalStateException used elsewhere in this class so the failure is explicit instead of a silent null count.

GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount can now return null after switching to modelSupplier.get() with a null check for concurrent deletion. — Null-return contract change in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount: the lookup switched from getGroupModel() to modelSupplier.get() with an added null check, so the method can now return null when the group is concurrently deleted (the underlying delegate lookup cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId()) returns null on concurrent deletion). The reviewer verified this introduces no stale-null memoization (LazyModel only caches non-null results), no downstream NPE (the only production caller, GroupUtils.toRepresentation, passes the value to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(Long) which accepts boxed Long), but the method's return contract is now nullable.

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition creates slug-less orgs when billing is off and grants slugs before payment when billing is on. — WHAT: The condition for setting the organization's `slug` was inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`, while the `requestedSlug` metadata condition was left unchanged. WHY: When team billing is disabled (self-hosted/OSS installs), organizations are now created with a null slug, breaking the org subdomain/URL; when billing is enabled, the slug is granted immediately at creation (bypassing the payment-gated flow where the slug should only live in metadata.requestedSlug until subscription, mirroring teams/create.handler.ts) and both slug and requestedSlug are set redundantly. This change is also unrelated to the PR's destinationCalendar purpose, suggesting an accidental edit. HOW: Restore the negated condition on the slug line: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`.

Empty-array destinationCalendar reaches EventManager.create's unguarded `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` and crashes confirmation of Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar. — WHAT: When neither the booking nor the confirming user has a destination calendar, the evt now carries `destinationCalendar: []`, which flows through handleConfirmation into EventManager.create where `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is followed by an unguarded `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` check (packages/core/EventManager.ts, the line right after the new @NOTE destructure).
