HOW: Guard the access in EventManager.create (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`), or omit the empty array here so consumers keep receiving null/undefined.

add_members/remove_member require params[:group_id] but the member route and JS client only provide params[:id], so both endpoints always raise ParameterMissing — WHAT: `add_members` (and identically `remove_member` at line 85) reads the group id via `params.require(:group_id)`, but the new routes (`delete "members"` / `put "members"` declared directly inside `resources :groups` in config/routes.rb:78-79) are member routes, so the group id arrives as `params[:id]`, and the JS client (discourse/models/group.js addMembers/removeMember) only sends `usernames`/`user_id` in the request body — `group_id` is never present. WHY: `params.require(:group_id)` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing on every request, so adding and removing group members from the admin UI always fails. HOW: use the member-route param: `group = Group.find(params[:id].to_i)` (or change the routes/JS to actually supply group_id).

group.users.delete is given an integer id instead of a User record, raising ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch — WHAT: `remove_member` passes an integer (`user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i`) to `group.users.delete(user_id)` on the `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association. WHY: ActiveRecord's collection delete runs `raise_on_type_mismatch` on each argument and raises ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch (User expected, got Fixnum), so removing a member 500s even once the group_id param issue is fixed. HOW: look up the record and delete the instance, e.g. `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` or reuse the existing `group.remove(user)` helper from app/models/group.rb.

totalPages uses floor+1 instead of ceil, producing a phantom empty last page whenever user_count is a multiple of limit — WHAT: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 users / limit 50 yields 3 pages instead of 2). WHY: on the real last page `showingLast` (currentPage == totalPages) stays false, so the next action runs and sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` = user_count, the server returns an empty member list, and the UI lands on a phantom empty page ("3/3"). HOW: use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (the user_count == 0 guard above already handles the empty case).

members list is rendered but findMembers() is never called on initial page load, so the admin group page shows no members until paging — WHAT: the template iterates `members` (`{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`), but a repo-wide grep for findMembers shows it is only invoked from the next/previous actions and after add/remove — nothing calls `model.findMembers()` when the admin group page is first rendered. WHY: the member list is empty on initial page load for an existing group (and the pager shows 0/0) until the admin clicks next/previous or adds/removes a member. HOW: call `findMembers()` when the route sets up the controller/model for an existing group (e.g. in the admin group route's setupController/afterModel).

Admin group template references itemView="group-member" but no GroupMemberView exists, crashing member list rendering and leaving the removeMember action untriggerable. — WHAT: The template renders group members with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, but no `GroupMemberView` (or `view:group-member` registration) exists anywhere in app/assets/javascripts — a repo-wide grep for `group-member|GroupMemberView` returns only this template line. WHY: Ember 1.x resolves the itemView string through the container when the {{each}} block instantiates item views; with no matching class it raises an assertion in debug builds and a createChildView(undefined) TypeError in production, so the admin group page render blows up as soon as `members` becomes non-empty (reachable today: `addMembers` succeeds server-side, then group.js calls `findMembers()` which populates `members` and forces the {{each}} to re-render). Additionally, the per-member UI that would trigger the controller's `removeMember` action has no view to live in, so members can never be removed from this page. HOW: add the missing view, e.g. `Discourse.GroupMemberView = Ember.View.extend({ templateName: 'admin/templates/group-member' })` with a remove button that calls `get('controller').send('removeMember', this.get('context'))`, or drop `itemView="group-member"` and render the remove control inline in the {{each}} block.

New hidden authn_use_chk inputs in passkeys.ftl have no JS consumer in the repo, making the block dead markup (or a missing JS counterpart) for the re-auth passkey flow. — WHAT: The new hidden 'authn_use_chk' inputs (credential IDs) rendered in the authn_select form have no consumer anywhere in the codebase — a repo-wide grep for 'authn_use_chk' returns only this template, and neither passkeysConditionalAuth.js nor webauthnAuthenticate.js (referenced below) reads them. WHY: If the accompanying JS that collects these credential IDs into the WebAuthn allowCredentials list is missing, the block is dead markup and the re-authentication passkey flow this PR intends to fix will still not restrict the assertion to the already-identified user's credentials; it also needlessly embeds the user's WebAuthn credential IDs in the page HTML. HOW: Verify passkeysConditionalAuth.js reads input[name="authn_use_chk"] to build allowCredentials when isUserIdentified is true; if no such consumer exists, either add it or remove this block.

PasswordForm.configuredFor now declares passkey-only (passwordless) users as configured for a required password step, which can strand them on an unsatisfiable password page if the template lacks the passkey UI. — WHAT: configuredFor now returns true for a user who has a passkey but NO password credential, and authenticate() renders the standard password page (createLoginPassword) after merely filling WebAuthn context data. WHY: For a REQUIRED PasswordForm execution, such users previously had configuredFor=false (routing to an alternative or required-action setup); now they land on a password field they cannot satisfy, and they can only proceed if the login-password template actually renders the passkey conditional-UI macro — if it does not, the user is hard-stuck in the flow. HOW: Ensure the login-password template includes the passkeys.ftl conditionalUIData macro (gated on enableWebAuthnConditionalUI), or only advertise configuredFor=true for passkey-only users when the password page can actually offer the passkey option.

Passkey conditional UI is now offered during re-authentication with no visible guard that the submitted passkey belongs to the already-identified user. — WHAT: fillContextForm is now invoked while context.getUser() is already set (re-authentication), and UsernamePasswordForm.action routes any passkey submission to webauthnAuth.action without any visible check that the asserted passkey belongs to the already-identified user. WHY: In a step-up/re-authentication flow, if WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator.action simply re-derives the user from the credential (its implementation is outside this change and could not be verified here), a passkey belonging to a different account would complete the re-authentication as that other identity, breaking identity continuity of the flow. HOW: In the passkey action path, when context.getUser() != null (re-auth), reject the assertion unless the credential's owning user equals context.getUser().

Direct subscript of integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for integrations whose metadata lacks a recorded sender, crashing the reinstall path with a 500. — WHAT: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is subscripted directly even though `build_integration` (lines 376-377) only sets `metadata["sender"]` conditionally (`if state.get("sender")`), and no code in src/sentry ever binds a `sender` pipeline state. WHY: on the reinstall path (Integration row exists without OrganizationIntegration — e.g., reinstall after uninstall leaves the Integration row behind), any integration whose metadata lacks "sender" (all integrations created before sender recording, or created via flows that never pass sender) raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html page — the new security check crashes open rather than failing closed. HOW: use safe access and treat a missing/unknown sender as a verification failure, e.g. `sender_login = integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` followed by `if not sender_login or pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != sender_login: return error(...)`.

Fresh-install path skips the authenticated-user-vs-installer check, letting an attacker claim an unrecorded GitHub App installation_id while authenticated as a different GitHub user. — WHAT: the fresh-install branch (`except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()`) completes the pipeline without ever comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user (`github_authenticated_user`, bound in OAuthLoginView) to the person who installed the GitHub App, while OAuthLoginView.bind_state("installation_id", ...) accepts an arbitrary installation_id from the query string (lines 397-399) before any state validation. WHY: the PR's stated guarantee — fail when the authenticated GitHub user differs from the app installer — is unenforced for installations not yet recorded in Sentry's DB, so anyone who obtains an unclaimed sentry-io app installation_id (abandoned direct-from-GitHub installs are never recorded; installation IDs are enumerable) can run the pipeline in their own session, authenticate as themselves, and attach the victim GitHub org's installation (with its repo access) to their own Sentry organization. HOW: on the DoesNotExist path, verify with the OAuth access token that the authenticated user can actually access the claimed installation (e.g., GitHub's GET /user/installations) before calling pipeline.next_step(), or fetch the installation via the GitHub App API and compare its account/events sender to github_authenticated_user.

Token exchange and GitHub /user fetch are unguarded, so network or API failures produce a 500 instead of the friendly installation-failed page. — WHAT: the OAuth token exchange (`safe_urlopen`, line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) sit outside the try/except that only wraps `safe_urlread`/payload parsing, so network failures to github.com or a non-200 from api.github.com/user raise instead of rendering the error page. WHY: transient GitHub unavailability, timeouts, or an expired/invalid access token turn a recoverable installation failure into an unhandled 500 during the setup pipeline, contradicting the PR's goal of gracefully failing the installation on verification problems. HOW: wrap the token exchange and get_user_info calls in the same (or a broader) try/except and fall through to `return error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

pipeline.signature has no definition anywhere in src/sentry (only these two new usages exist), so the OAuth step either crashes with AttributeError or, if defined elsewhere as a provider-static hash, the state check binds nothing per-session. — WHAT: `pipeline.signature` is read at lines 402 and 412, but a bare-word search across all of src/sentry finds no definition of `signature` anywhere — no property, class attribute, or annotation on Pipeline or elsewhere; the only occurrences in the entire tree are these two new usages. WHY: if the attribute does not exist, the first dispatch of OAuthLoginView raises AttributeError and the GitHub installation flow 500s immediately, before any redirect to GitHub; and even if it is defined outside the indexed tree with the usual upstream semantics (md5 of the provider key), the value is a static per-provider constant, so the `state` check at line 412 validates nothing per-session and provides no CSRF/session binding for the OAuth callback. HOW: verify that Pipeline actually defines `signature`; if not, add a per-session nonce (e.g., generate a random token, store it via pipeline.bind_state, and compare against it on callback) instead of relying on a missing or provider-static value.

Call to non-existent AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken breaks compilation of the new encoder provider. — WHAT: Line 54 calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), but a repo-wide search for 'ShouldUseLightweightToken' matches only this call site — the method does not exist in AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper or anywhere else. WHY: The module fails to compile, so no access token can be issued; if the method is added by a companion change it must be merged together, otherwise initToken (TokenManager.java:1053) is dead code. HOW: Add a static getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession) helper to AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper (or call the existing lightweight-token check used elsewhere) before relying on it here.

New factory implements a missing interface and calls missing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut(), breaking compilation and provider wiring. — WHAT: This factory references two symbols that do not exist in the codebase: (a) TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory in the implements clause (line 36) — no such interface file exists (TokenContextEncoderProvider.java declares only the provider interface), and (b) OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (import line 31, used at lines 72, 110, 126-128) including calls to getShortcut(), which is declared nowhere in the org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants package. WHY: The code does not compile, and because the SPI factory interface/registration is missing, TokenManager.initToken's session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) (TokenManager.java:1052) would return null and NPE on every access-token issuance even if compilation were fixed. HOW: Add the TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory interface (extending ProviderFactory<TokenContextEncoderProvider>) plus its provider-factory registration, and add getShortcut() to the grant-type factory SPI (or look the shortcut up from an existing source) as part of this PR.

Grant-type context is only wired for the refresh flow, so all initially issued tokens encode grantType as 'na'. — WHAT: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set on the ClientSessionContext only in validateToken (refresh flow, line 248); a repo-wide search for setAttribute(.*GRANT_TYPE finds no other setter, so the grantType read by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (line 57) is null for every initial token issuance and is encoded as 'na'. WHY: Access tokens issued via authorization_code, client_credentials, password, device, token-exchange, etc. all carry grant-type 'na' — the PR's advertised grant-type context only ever works for tokens created by refresh, and the grantType field newly captured in OAuth2GrantType.Context (line 102) is never consumed. HOW: In the grant processing path (e.g., AbstractOIDCGrantType/TokenEndpoint where clientSessionCtx is built), propagate the grant type — for example clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) — before TokenManager.initToken runs.

Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId. — WHAT: The constructor checks Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") at line 73, duplicating the grantType check from line 72 and never validating rawTokenId. WHY: A null rawTokenId is silently accepted despite the guard's intent, producing '...:null'-style encoded ids or NPEs later in encodeTokenId string concatenation semantics, and the exception message is misleading when grantType is null. HOW: Change line 73 to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

Refresh flow sets grantType="refresh_token", which has no registered OAuth2GrantType shortcut, so encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException and every refresh-token request fails. — WHAT: The refresh flow sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN ("refresh_token") on the client session context, but no OAuth2GrantType provider with id "refresh_token" exists anywhere in the codebase (repo-wide grep shows zero OAuth2GrantType implementations/factories), so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType("refresh_token") always returns null and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException("Cannot encode token with unknown grantType: refresh_token") at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:111. WHY: Once the encoder provider is wired in, every refresh-token request reaches initToken → getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext → encodeTokenId and fails with a 500, completely breaking the refresh-token grant — the one flow this PR annotates with a real grant type (all other flows fall back to the registered "na" shortcut and encode fine). HOW: Either register a refresh_token OAuth2GrantType implementation with a 2-char shortcut so the factory maps resolve it, or make encodeTokenId fall back to the UNKNOWN ("na") shortcut instead of throwing when getShortcutByGrantType returns null, e.g. `String grantShort = factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType()); if (grantShort == null) { grantShort = UNKNOWN; }`.

New ruler-less list view can never show Delete/Pause menu items and Silence is a no-op because AlertRuleMenu and the silence drawer still require the rulerRule that the list no longer fetches. — WHAT: The new ruler-less list view renders RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu without a rulerRule, but the downstream components still gate actions on the ruler rule: AlertRuleMenu renders Delete only when `canDelete && rulerRule` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165) and Pause only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123), and RuleActionsButtons.V2 mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104) — all false when rulerRule is undefined. WHY: In the new alert list view the Delete and Pause menu items never appear (making the newly added grafanaDeleteAbility/grafanaPauseAbility dead code), and clicking 'Silence notifications' sets showSilenceDrawer=true but the drawer never mounts, so silencing from the list view silently does nothing — a functional regression versus the previous list which passed the ruler rule. HOW: Thread a pause/silence/delete capability that works from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (e.g., relax the guards to also accept the grafana prom rule path: render Delete when canDelete using the identifier-based delete modal, and support SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer/MenuItemPauseRule from promRule), or keep these abilities disabled in the list until the UI supports them.

Refactored useAllAlertRuleAbilities loses the isFederatedRuleGroup check, making federated Mimir rule groups appear editable/removable. — WHAT: The refactored useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` — dropping the previous `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);` check that made rules in federated (Mimir) rule groups immutable. WHY: For federated rule groups, Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently abilities are now reported as supported whenever the ruler is available and the user is editable/removable, so the UI can offer edit/delete/pause on federated rules that must not be modified through this cluster (previously blocked via immutableRule). HOW: Restore the federated detection — e.g., compute `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in useAllAlertRuleAbilities and pass it (or the CombinedRuleGroup) into useAllRulerRuleAbilities so immutableRule still includes federated groups.

skipToken path in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still reports Duplicate as supported, which can wrongly enable Duplicate for cloud rules when their ruler is unavailable. — WHAT: When callers pass skipToken (rule is undefined — used by AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons.V2 for non-Grafana prom rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still returns Duplicate as [AlwaysSupported, grafanaRulesPermissions.create] because `loading` from useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined) is false, making MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported. WHY: In AlertRuleMenu the abilities are OR'ed (`canDuplicate = (ruler…) || (grafana…)`), so for a data-source (Mimir/Cortex) rule whose ruler is unavailable or still loading — where the ruler-based duplicate ability is NotSupported — the Duplicate menu item is now shown to any user with Grafana alert-rules create permission; previously it was hidden until the ruler was available. HOW: Short-circuit when the rule is undefined/skipToken so every action returns [NotSupported, false] (e.g., in useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities return a disabled abilities object when `rule === skipToken`).

New prom-based abilities hook restricts ModifyExport to alerting rules, hiding the Export action for Grafana-managed recording rules in the ruler-less list view. — WHAT: The new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), which returns false for recording rules, while the old ruler-based code gated it on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) (true for any Grafana-managed rule, including recording rules — see the removed hunk '[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]'). WHY: In the new ruler-less list view (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, so rulerRule is undefined and the ruler fallback in AlertRuleMenu yields supported=false), Grafana-managed recording rules lose the Export menu action that was previously available — a silent feature regression, since exporting recording rules to provisioning format is supported. HOW: Use the any-grafana-rule guard for ModifyExport, e.g. '[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), exportAllowed]' (keeping the alerting-only restriction only for Pause/Restore where it is semantically correct).

Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma.credential.update without importing prisma, breaking the whole integration. — WHAT: `prisma.credential.update` is called at line 96 but `prisma` is never imported in this file (the imports at lines 1-20 contain no prisma import). WHY: every Salesforce calendar operation constructs this service, so getClient throws a ReferenceError ('prisma is not defined') — or fails TypeScript compilation — making the entire Salesforce integration unusable. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` to the imports.

Salesforce connection is built with the stale access token even though a fresh one was just refreshed and saved. — WHAT: after fetching fresh tokens (lines 75-99), the jsforce.Connection is constructed with the OLD `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`/`instance_url`. WHY: this code path runs because the stored access token is expired, so the connection is initialized with a token Salesforce will reject with 401; the freshly refreshed token that was just saved to the DB is never used for this session. HOW: use the parsed fresh values when building the connection, e.g. `instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url, accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

Webhook filters/ creates credentials by appMetadata.slug which is undefined, so Prisma ignores the appId filter and overwrites an arbitrary credential of the user. — WHAT: the credential lookup/create uses `appMetadata.slug`, but app-store metadata objects have no `slug` property (verified: no `slug:` in appStoreMetaData.ts or any app `_metadata.ts`), so `appId` is `undefined`. WHY: Prisma silently drops `undefined` fields from `where`, so `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: undefined } })` matches the user's FIRST credential of ANY app and `update` overwrites that credential's key with the synced keys — syncing one app corrupts another app's stored credentials; the create path likewise writes a credential with a missing appId. HOW: use the key that was used for the lookup, e.g. `appId: app.slug` (the App table slug that indexed appStoreMetadata), instead of `appMetadata.slug`.

Office365 passes a hyphenated appSlug that will not match the App table slug, breaking the credential-sync callback. — WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with appSlug "office365-calendar", but the app-store metadata key / App table slug for this integration is "office365calendar" (no hyphen — matching how zoomvideo passes "zoomvideo" and webex passes "webex"). WHY: the credential-sync endpoint echoes this appSlug back to the new /api/webhook/app-credential handler, which does `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })` — "office365-calendar" matches no App row, so the sync callback 404s and Office 365 token sync never persists. HOW: pass "office365calendar" as the appSlug.

Webex wraps refresh in refreshOAuthTokens but still parses with the full Webex token schema, so sync-mode responses always fail validation. — WHAT: the refresh fetch is now wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, whose sync-mode branch returns the sync endpoint's response containing only an access token and expiry (per its own doc comment), but the response is still parsed with the strict `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` (requires `scope` literal, `token_type` literal, `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`). WHY: when credential sharing is enabled, the parse always fails and refreshAccessToken rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex meeting creation breaks for synced credentials. HOW: route the response through `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, webexRefreshedTokenSchema)` like zoom/office365 do, or skip the strict schema when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is active.

In sync mode the Zoom refresh writes expiry_date = NaN because the stripped parse result has no expires_in, permanently breaking Zoom token parsing afterwards. — WHAT: switching to `parseRefreshTokenResponse` means that in credential-sync mode the parsed data only contains `access_token` (plus an injected placeholder `refresh_token`); `expires_in` is stripped, so the unchanged line below computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN and stores it. WHY: on the next getToken call, `zoomTokenSchema.parse(credential.key)` rejects NaN for `expiry_date: z.number()`, so every Zoom operation fails with "Zoom credential keys parsing error" once a synced refresh has occurred. HOW: when expires_in is absent, use the expiry returned by the sync endpoint or leave the previous expiry_date unchanged instead of writing NaN.

Webhook throws unhandled ZodError/decrypt exceptions on bad input instead of returning a 400. — WHAT: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31) and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (lines 57-59) throw on malformed input with no try/catch. WHY: any request that passes the secret check but has an invalid body shape, undecryptable payload, or non-JSON decrypted content produces an unhandled 500 (and in some Next.js setups an HTML error page) instead of a clean 4xx, which also breaks the calling sync service's error handling. HOW: use `safeParse` and return 400 on failure, and wrap the decrypt/JSON.parse in a try/catch returning 400.

Salesforce refresh relies on response.statusText === "OK" which is not guaranteed (empty under HTTP/2). — WHAT: token refresh success is detected via `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of checking `response.ok`/status code. WHY: `statusText` is an empty string on HTTP/2 responses (Node fetch/undici), so a successful Salesforce token response can be misclassified as an error and throw HttpError 400; conversely it couples correctness to an optional protocol detail. HOW: use `if (!response.ok) throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText || String(response.status) });`.

Webhook findFirst→create is a TOCTOU race with no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId), allowing duplicate credentials whose stale copies are never updated again. — WHAT: the findFirst-then-create sequence is a check-then-act race — the Credential model (schema.prisma:253-272) has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), only plain indexes, so two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app both find no row and both insert a credential. WHY: duplicate Credential rows are created for the same user/app, and because this handler (and Cal.com generally) reads credentials via findFirst, only one row is ever updated/read afterwards — the duplicate keeps stale keys indefinitely with no way to reconcile. HOW: perform the lookup-and-write inside a serializable transaction (prisma.$transaction with isolationLevel: 'Serializable') and retry on serialization failure, or add a @@unique([userId, appId]) constraint (after dedup) and switch to upsert on that compound key.

Credential update path does not clear the invalid flag, so syncing fresh keys never revives a credential previously marked invalid after a failed refresh. — WHAT: the update branch only writes `key` and never resets the credential's `invalid` flag, even though Cal.com sets credential.invalid = true when a token refresh fails (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:368, webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:305, googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:115). WHY: a user whose credential was marked invalid receives fresh, working keys from the parent app store, but the credential stays flagged invalid, so Cal.com continues treating the integration as broken — the sync silently fails to restore it, defeating the purpose of the endpoint for exactly the credentials that most need re-syncing. HOW: add invalid: false to the update data so a successful key sync revives the credential.

align-items mixin is missing -moz-box-align, so the Gecko box fallback provided by flexbox() never receives cross-axis alignment. — WHAT: The align-items mixin omits the -moz-box-align declaration while its sibling mixins flexbox() and order() both include old-Gecko fallbacks (display: -moz-box, -moz-box-ordinal-group). WHY: On browsers that receive the -moz-box display fallback (old Firefox), flex items are never cross-axis aligned — the header contents, small-action rows, and bullet badges this PR converts will not be vertically centered/baselined there, contradicting the PR's stated 'all prefixes' goal. HOW: Add the Gecko box-align line to the mixin.

Button inside the newly-flexed .small-action keeps float:right, which flex items ignore, so it loses its right-edge alignment. — WHAT: .small-action is converted to a flex container (@include flexbox()) but its child 'button { float: right; }' rule (lines 555-559) was not migrated — floats have no effect on flex items, and unlike .panel in header.scss the button was not given 'margin-left: auto'. WHY: Any button rendered directly inside .small-action (the rule's existence implies one exists) will stop being right-aligned and will instead sit immediately after .small-action-desc, a layout regression for small-action posts. HOW: Mirror the pattern this PR already used for .panel by adding margin-left: auto to the button rule.

Removing the float fallbacks for .title/.panel leaves the header unlaid-out (panel stacked below title) in browsers with no flexbox support. — WHAT: The float fallbacks (.title { float: left; } and .panel { float: right; }) were removed and replaced with flex-only positioning (margin-left: auto on .panel, order on .panel/.extra-info-wrapper), which only takes effect when one of the five flex display values from flexbox() is supported. WHY: On any browser with no flexbox support at all (e.g., IE9, which the -ms-flexbox prefix does not cover), .title and .panel become plain block elements — the panel/login buttons drop below the logo at full width, breaking the header layout; keeping the floats would have been a zero-cost fallback since floats are ignored on flex items. HOW: Retain 'float: left' on .title and 'float: right' on .panel alongside the new flex rules.

LoggerMiddleware now depends on the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware being wired ahead of it (no wiring change is present in this diff) and permanently drops the traceID field from the plugin request log. — WHAT: logRequest now sources pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname exclusively from m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only works if the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs before LoggerMiddleware in the client middleware chain, and the explicit traceID extraction (tracing.TraceIDFromContext) was deleted with no replacement in instrumentContext. WHY: the diff registers NewContextualLoggerMiddleware nowhere (grep finds zero call sites for it and for NewMetricsMiddleware), so if the chain assembly is not updated in tandem — and ordered with ContextualLoggerMiddleware above LoggerMiddleware — the 'Plugin Request Completed' egress log silently loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname, and traceID is lost unconditionally even with correct wiring since neither the logger middleware nor instrumentContext adds it anymore. HOW: in the middleware chain assembly (pluginsintegration wiring), replace NewInstrumentationMiddleware with NewMetricsMiddleware AND insert NewContextualLoggerMiddleware at the top of the stack, ahead of NewLoggerMiddleware; additionally either have instrumentContext append the traceID (tracing.TraceIDFromContext) or keep the explicit traceID logParam in logRequest.

Adding FromContext to the plog.Logger interface is a breaking change for any other implementers (fakes/test doubles) that were not updated in this diff. — WHAT: the Logger interface gained a new required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger, but only grafanaInfraLogWrapper (pkg/plugins/log/logger.go) implements it in the visible code. WHY: any other type that implements plog.Logger (fakes/test doubles used by plugin manager tests or alternative loggers) no longer satisfies the interface and fails compilation with 'missing method FromContext' — I searched the repo for other implementations and could not confirm none exist outside this snapshot. HOW: add FromContext to every existing Logger implementation (a safe default is `func (f *Fake) FromContext(context.Context) Logger { return f }`), or verify via a full build that grafanaInfraLogWrapper is the only implementer.

Required destination/attempts fields reject all Working Draft-format browser reports with 422, contradicting the stated 'support both specs' intent. — WHAT: `destination` and `attempts` are declared as required serializer fields, but the W3C Working Draft report format (https://www.w3.org/TR/reporting-1/, cited in the comment directly above) defines only type/url/user_agent/body/age — `destination` and `attempts` are Editor's Draft additions, and only `age`/`timestamp` were made optional. WHY: browsers sending Working-Draft-style reports (with `age`, without `destination`/`attempts`) fail validation and get HTTP 422, so this experimental data-collection endpoint drops exactly the real-world reports it exists to gather. HOW: make the non-overlapping fields optional, e.g. `destination = serializers.CharField(required=False)` and `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(required=False, min_value=1)`, matching the age/timestamp handling.

Field-level age/timestamp validators never run when the field is absent, so reports with neither age nor timestamp validate successfully despite both specs requiring one. — WHAT: `validate_age` and `validate_timestamp` are field-level validators that only run when their respective field is present in the input, so a report containing neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation — the docstring contract 'Validate that age is present' can never be enforced by a validator that is skipped when age is absent. WHY: both cited specs require exactly one of `age` (Working Draft) or `timestamp` (Editor's Draft), so structurally incomplete reports are accepted and counted as valid browser reports. HOW: replace the two field validators with an object-level `validate(self, attrs)` that raises ValidationError unless exactly one of age/timestamp is present.

A single invalid report aborts the whole batch with 422 before any valid reports are processed, dropping all valid telemetry in the batch. — WHAT: on the first invalid report in a batch the endpoint returns 422 immediately, before the metrics loop over `validated_reports` runs, so every valid report in the same batch is dropped without being recorded. WHY: browsers send reports as batched arrays, and one malformed or unknown-typed report (e.g., a report type not yet in BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) poisons the entire batch, silently losing telemetry this collector exists to capture. HOW: skip invalid reports (log and `continue`) and still process the valid ones, reserving 422 only for payloads where nothing is processable.

Import of non-existent `sentry.api.fields.actor.ActorField` breaks module import for all detector endpoints — WHAT: `from sentry.api.fields.actor import ActorField` imports a class that does not exist anywhere in the repository — there is no `actor.py` under `src/sentry/api/fields`, no `class ActorField` definition repo-wide, and no other file imports anything from `sentry.api.fields.<submodule>`. WHY: importing this validator module raises ModuleNotFoundError at import time, so every workflow_engine endpoint that imports `BaseDetectorTypeValidator` fails to load (broken create/update detector endpoints). HOW: add `src/sentry/api/fields/actor.py` defining `ActorField` (returning an object with `is_user`/`is_team`/`id`, as the owner-handling code expects), or remove the import and the owner feature.

Runtime-unsubscriptable `serializers.Serializer[Any]` raises TypeError at import, breaking the collector endpoint module — WHAT: `class BrowserReportSerializer(serializers.Serializer[Any])` subscripts DRF's `Serializer` in a base-class list, which is evaluated at runtime; stock DRF serializers do not define `__class_getitem__`, this is the only runtime-subscripted serializer in the entire codebase, and no `django_stubs_ext`/monkeypatch is enabled anywhere in the repo. WHY: raises `TypeError: type 'Serializer' is not subscriptable` at module import time, so the browser reporting collector endpoint module fails to load. HOW: drop the subscript — `class BrowserReportSerializer(serializers.Serializer):` (the `[Any]` parameterization adds nothing at runtime here).

Mutated config copy is discarded; the returned monitor context uses the original config so the schedule_type display substitution never takes effect (carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py). — WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context builds config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy() and substitutes the human-readable schedule_type into that copy, but the returned dict uses monitor_environment.monitor.config (the original), so the mutation is silently discarded and the copy is dead code. WHY: the emitted monitor context in the occurrence event payload keeps the raw integer schedule_type instead of the display value the code intends, and the misleading copy/mutate pattern invites future edits to the wrong object. NOTE: this defect was carried over verbatim from the deleted get_monitor_environment_context in mark_failed.py — it is pre-existing, not introduced by this refactor, but it now lives in these added lines. HOW: return the mutated copy in the payload.

get_monitor_environment_context drops the schedule_type substitution by returning the raw monitor config instead of the display-substituted copy it computed. — get_monitor_environment_context computes a display-substituted copy of the monitor config but then returns monitor_environment.monitor.config, so the schedule_type substitution is silently dropped from the context. Return the substituted copy instead. Per the analysis, this is a pre-existing bug moved verbatim by the refactor (not introduced or worsened by it) and was already reported in the prior pass.

Unguarded prisma update inside the catch block can throw and abort the entire SMS scheduling cron run. — WHAT: the catch block now performs an unguarded prisma.workflowReminder.update; if it throws, the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: the most common reason for entering the catch is a database/connectivity failure (or the reminder row was already removed by a concurrent cron run's deleteMany), so the retry-count update is likely to throw too — aborting processing of all remaining reminders and failing the whole cron run with a 500, whereas before this PR the catch only logged and continued to the next reminder. The same double-fault occurs when the else-branch update throws, since catch then re-runs the identical failing update. HOW: wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch (or use updateMany + increment so a missing row is a no-op) so one reminder's failure cannot abort the run.

retryCount>1 delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders, so the SMS cron can delete reminders of other methods. — WHAT: the new OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } in the deleteMany dropped the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter (and has no scheduled filter), so this SMS cron now deletes workflow reminders of any method once their retryCount exceeds 1. WHY: the original cleanup was explicitly scoped to SMS reminders; as written, any current or future code path that increments retryCount on non-SMS (e.g. EMAIL) reminders — or an SMS reminder that later got scheduled — would have those rows silently deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. Today only this handler increments retryCount so the impact is latent, but the clause contradicts the intended SMS-only scope. HOW: keep the method filter inside the retryCount branch: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }.

Stale read-modify-write of retryCount loses increments under overlapping cron runs; use atomic increment. — WHAT: retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 is a non-atomic read-modify-write using the value fetched at the start of the run. WHY: if two cron executions overlap (or the same run retries), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1 instead of N+2, so a failing reminder gets more than the intended two scheduling attempts before being deleted — the exact unbounded-rescheduling behavior this PR aims to eliminate. HOW: use Prisma's atomic increment: data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } in both the else branch and the catch branch.

The catch block's retryCount-incrementing database update is unguarded. — Unguarded update in the catch block: the catch handler performs a database update (incrementing retryCount) without guarding that update itself. This is one of the three pre-existing findings the analysis reaffirms; it is located in the new else/catch logic within the changed hunk at lines 267-286.

The deleteMany OR-branch omits the `method: SMS` filter, broadening which reminders get deleted. — The deleteMany call's OR branch drops the `method: SMS` filter, so the deletion is no longer restricted to SMS-method reminders. This is one of the three pre-existing findings the analysis reaffirms; no file path or line numbers for the deleteMany are given in the analysis.

retryCount is updated via a non-atomic read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment. — Non-atomic retryCount read-modify-write: retryCount is read from the fetched reminder and then written back as a separate incremented update rather than via an atomic operation, making it race-prone. This is one of the three pre-existing findings the analysis reaffirms; the increment occurs in the catch logic of the changed hunk at lines 267-286.

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is never True for spawn-context children, so hung flusher processes are never killed before a duplicate replacement is started. — WHAT: `process.kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is gated behind `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but the flusher spawns children via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which returns `SpawnProcess` instances — a sibling of `ForkProcess` (what `multiprocessing.Process` resolves to with the default fork context on Linux/Python 3.13), not a subclass. WHY: the isinstance check is always False in production, so a hung flusher child (the `"hang"` path, where `is_alive()` is still True) is never killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement — two live processes then flush the same shards concurrently, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and racing `done_flush_segments` deletions, while the dead/hung process leaks and `process_restarts` escalates to RuntimeError. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this is a regression. HOW: check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess)` (or `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`), or simply attempt `process.kill()` in the try/except as before — threads (test mode) are already excluded by the missing attribute, which the new `except (ValueError, AttributeError)` handles.

Inconsistent metrics tag key ("shards" vs "shard") between the two newly added flusher timers breaks per-shard grouping. — WHAT: The newly added `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer uses tag key `"shards"` while the sibling `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timing added in the same loop use `"shard"` for the identical `shard_tag` value. WHY: metrics for the same per-process flush cycle cannot be grouped or filtered under one tag key — dashboards/alerts keyed on `shard` silently exclude the wait_produce series, degrading the per-shard observability this PR is adding. HOW: use the same tag key `"shard"` in the wait_produce timer.

Removing the global BuildIndex lock without adding per-key synchronization allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same index, racing bleve.New on the same on-disk directory and leaking the overwritten index. — WHAT: Removing the function-wide b.cacheMu from BuildIndex leaves only the final cache write locked, but neither getOrCreateIndex (search.go:287-313) nor build takes any per-key lock, so two concurrent Search/handleEvent calls for the same uncached NamespacedResource now run BuildIndex in parallel for the same key. WHY: for file-based indexes both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory (racing index creation on disk, risking corruption/error), both execute the full expensive document build this PR is trying to speed up, and both assign b.cache[key] — last write wins and the losing bleve.Index is never Close()d, leaking file handles and scorch goroutines. HOW: guard against duplicate concurrent builds, e.g. use singleflight or a per-key mutex keyed by NamespacedResource around the build, or re-check b.cache under the write lock before overwriting and Close() the superseded index.

New TotalDocs() call in init races with watch-triggered BuildIndex cache writes because TotalDocs reads the index cache map without holding cacheMu. — WHAT: The new 'search index initialized' log calls s.search.TotalDocs() after the WatchWriteEvents goroutine has already been started, and bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:203-213) iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu while the watch goroutine can concurrently trigger BuildIndex, which writes b.cache[key]. WHY: concurrent map read (TotalDocs) and map write (BuildIndex cache insert) is a data race that the Go runtime turns into a fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' crash, and events can arrive immediately because the SQL backend streams recent write events on a new watch. HOW: take b.cacheMu.RLock() inside bleveBackend.TotalDocs (and any other cache iteration), or move the log/TotalDocs call before the watch goroutine is started.

Postgres skip added in the same PR that introduces DB-backed init at server startup removes CI coverage for exactly the path being changed. — WHAT: The PR skips TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer on postgres with a TODO, in the same PR that makes ResourceServer run full DB-backed initialization (GetResourceStats, index builds, WatchWriteEvents) at startup. WHY: this removes the only CI coverage exercising the storage-server target against postgres exactly when the new startup-init path is introduced, so a postgres-specific init failure (the test 'works locally' but fails in Drone, suggesting an environment-dependent startup defect) ships undetected. HOW: fix the Drone postgres environment for this test (or gate only the failing assertion) instead of skipping the whole target test, and re-enable before merging the startup-init change.

Starting the event watcher only after the search index build completes drops all write events committed during the build, leaving the index permanently stale for those resources. — WHAT: Moving initWatcher() to run after search.init(ctx) opens a gap where write events are permanently lost from the search index: WatchWriteEvents (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:558-566) snapshots the latest RVs via listLatestRVs at watcher start and its poller only streams events with RV greater than that snapshot, while each index build lists resources at fetchLatestRV (backend.go:476) captured at build time. WHY: any write committed after a resource's index-build snapshot but before the watcher starts is neither included in the built index nor delivered to handleEvent, so those resources are missing/stale in search results indefinitely (until they happen to be modified again); the window lasts the entire startup index build, which this PR itself notes is slow, and coincides with startup provisioning writes. The previous order (watcher first, then build) was safe because it produced overlap, and index writes are idempotent upserts keyed by resource. HOW: start the watcher before building the indexes again, or capture the build's list RVs and start the watch from those RVs so the two coverages overlap instead of gap.
